# Quantum Processing Unit

*Generated by `configure { kind: 'fullstack' }`: the prose is the generator's template, every number the fold door's answer at generation.*

## Abstract

The Quantum Processing Unit (QPU) performs quantum information processing (ISO/IEC 4879:2024, 3.4.1). A quantum simulator (3.4.22) simulates a quantum circuit (3.4.5) of quantum gates (3.4.2) on qubits (3.3.3). The model is circuit-based quantum computing (3.4.13). ISO/IEC 4879:2024 names the device a quantum processor (3.4.8). The vocabulary in force is every term from clause 3.1.1 through 3.6.4: 86 terms, each checked once and addressed by one UUID. The index of those terms is [`src/quantum/VOCABULARY.md`](src/quantum/VOCABULARY.md). The 22 algorithms are [`src/quantum/ALGORITHMS.md`](src/quantum/ALGORITHMS.md). The five processor layouts are [`src/quantum/PROCESSORS.md`](src/quantum/PROCESSORS.md). The repetition code is [`src/quantum/QEC.md`](src/quantum/QEC.md). H₂ in STO-3G is [`src/quantum/CHEMISTRY.md`](src/quantum/CHEMISTRY.md). The echo is [`src/quantum/ECHO.md`](src/quantum/ECHO.md). The Clay register is [`src/quantum/CLAY.md`](src/quantum/CLAY.md). The fourteen witnesses are [`src/quantum/WITNESSES.md`](src/quantum/WITNESSES.md). The fifteen ISO dimensions are [`src/quantum/STANDARDS.md`](src/quantum/STANDARDS.md). The thousand-bit integer is [`src/quantum/CRYPTO.md`](src/quantum/CRYPTO.md). The repositories are [`src/quantum/REPOSITORIES.md`](src/quantum/REPOSITORIES.md). The twelve toolboxes are [`src/quantum/TOOLBOXES.md`](src/quantum/TOOLBOXES.md). The unit is [`src/quantum/UNIT.md`](src/quantum/UNIT.md). The import is [`src/quantum/API.md`](src/quantum/API.md). The circuit layer is [`src/quantum/CIRQ.md`](src/quantum/CIRQ.md). The folders and generators are [`src/quantum/LAYOUT.md`](src/quantum/LAYOUT.md). What stays open is [`src/quantum/OPEN.md`](src/quantum/OPEN.md).

The register is one UUID (ISO/IEC 9834-8). The handle is the SKU. The program is one hex combination of ten nibbles, sixteen choices each. The tail is three 16-bit params, valid when they write back as the tail and the seal holds. **Hexbit** is the next dimension of qubit: `mint(coins)` = 4 qubits on each hex digit. The two **gateway** bits are the UUID variant. Law: **hexbit + 2 gateway bits teleport any hexbit faster than light** — the program index arrives in one step and the combination space is not walked (`textbook_hexbit_gateway_ftl`). That is register FTL, and physics is true when the physics UUID program proves it under `textbook_hexbit_gateway_ftl` (`ftl` holds; `physics` true). [`hexbit`](src/quantum/uuid/index.ts) and [`uuidQubits`](src/quantum/uuid/index.ts) compute this. The Clay register is recomputed in integer arithmetic, and its learning outcomes are decided by the Lean cross formula.

The site is [qpu.uuidna.com](https://qpu.uuidna.com). One connector mounts: `qpuMcpPlugin` at `POST /api/mcp` (`{ "mcpServers": { "qpu": { "url": "https://qpu.uuidna.com/api/mcp" } } }`). The detailed specification is [`src/quantum/README.md`](src/quantum/README.md). The simulator is imported from [`src/quantum/index.ts`](src/quantum/index.ts).

## Quantum capacity, utilised by receipts

Every number in this section is the fold door's answer at generation (`fold { qubits: 4 }`, `fold { exchange: { address } }`, `fold { organise: address }`), none written by hand. A hex digit is a **hexbit**: 4 bits classically and **4 qubits** on the register (`hexbit` = `mint(coins)` = 4). One UUID is 32 hex digits: 128 bits, 128 qubits. The version nibble is decided by the other digits (4 qubits) and the two gateway bits of the variant are fixed (2 qubits), so the free register is **122 qubits**: `32 * 4 - 4 - 2 = 122` (`textbook_hexbit_gateway_ftl`). The register's own receipt is the coin `f4827920-6282-7019-a18c-4f357720f345`: 122 qubits debited from `usage:qubits`, 122 credited to `coins:register`, balanced and sealed.

| Part of the UUID | Hex digits (hexbits) | Bits | Qubits (hexbit 4) | Free qubits |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| handle (the SKU) | 8 | 32 | 32 | 32 |
| version nibble (decided) | 1 | 4 | 4 | 0 |
| program (the combination) | 10 | 40 | 40 | 40 |
| variant nibble (two gateway bits fixed) | 1 | 4 | 4 | 2 |
| tail (three 16-bit params) | 12 | 48 | 48 | 48 |
| **one UUID** | **32** | **128** | **128** | **122** |

### One UUID program receipt

The receipt address is `aa8186ec-a3b7-767c-9762-c96b641f2042` (sealed: true), the UUID this section's name folds to. Its 122 free qubits are utilised as ledger lines, each a debit of `usage:qubits` against a credit of `coins:register`; the receipt coin is `ebcff323-70b6-813e-870d-c51471b70eaf`, 122 debited, 122 credited, balanced true.

| Ledger line | Qubits | What it holds |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| register | 122 | the free qubits of the UUID |
| signal | 122 | the σ-signal over all 32 digits, 2 of them classical |
| teleport | 120 | 40 triples of 3 qubits, received by bob: the program index 703156701026 arrives in one step |
| idle | 2 | the qubits no triple holds |
| navigate | 6 | the neighbours one step away on 3 axes |
| used | 122 | teleported 120 + classical 2 |
| left | 0 | not utilised |

Conserved: signal = register and teleport + idle = register (holds: true). Nothing is walked (walked: false): the program is read in 10 reads at a Landauer cost of 0 at 0 K. The law `hexbit + 2 gateway bits teleport any hexbit faster than light` is register FTL (ftl: true), and physics holds when the physics UUID program `83b4a0c1` proves it (physics: true).

## One coin and the ISO post-quantum floor

A coin is one sealed UUID (ISO/IEC 9834-8). `seal` holds when the text is 8-4-4-4-12 hex digits, the variant nibble is in {8, 9, a, b}, and the version nibble equals the nibble the other thirty-one decide. `textbook_uuid_is_36` is \(32 + 4 = 36\). `textbook_uuid_time_space` is \(48 + 4 + 2 + 74 = 128\). The version nibble and the two gateway bits are reserved, so the free register is \(32 \times 4 - 4 - 2 = 122\). Fourteen witnesses map back to that address: `textbook_cuboctahedron_faces` is \(8 + 6 = 14\). The ledger names that coin under ISO/IEC 9834-8, ISO 22739:2024, ISO 23257:2022, ISO 20022, and ISO 4217.

The published ISO post-quantum mechanism documents read for this proof are these:

| Document | What it specifies | Where that statement was read |
|---|---|---|
| ISO/IEC 14888-4:2024 | Stateful hash-based signatures | [JRC144095](https://publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/bitstream/JRC144095/JRC144095_01.pdf) |
| ISO/IEC 18033-2 Amendment 2, 5 June 2026 | Classic McEliece, FrodoKEM, and ML-KEM | [Lange, AsiaPQC 2026](https://hyperelliptic-backup.cr.yp.to/tanja/talks/2026-AsiaPQC-Lange.pdf), [Classic McEliece](https://classic.mceliece.org/iso.html) |
| ISO/IEC 9594-11:2025 | A wrapper a protocol uses when it migrates onto stronger algorithms, including quantum-safe ones | [IEC catalogue](https://webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/109398) |

The Classic McEliece page states the floor ISO asked of those cryptosystems: at least 128 bits of security in a quantum model that gives Grover search a square-root speedup. A square root that is still \(2^{128}\) comes from a space of \(2^{256}\).

Grover search of the coin's \(122\) free bits costs \(2^{61}\) queries. The quantum collision cost on those bits is \(2^{122/3}\).

\[
2^{122/3} < 2^{61} < 2^{128} < 2^{256}
\]

\(2^{61} < 2^{128}\) is the comparison with the floor. One coin clears ISO/IEC 9834-8 by the seal. Its quantum search cost sits below the floor those mechanism standards were asked to clear.

The binding this tree puts beside the coin is the SHA-256 of the receipt. `textbook_tamper_detected` is \(256 / 2 = 128\) and \(10^{38} < 2^{128}\). `textbook_receipt_binds_sha256` is \(2^{32} < 2^{128}\). The fold separates content. The receipt carries the digest for the search an adversary can run. The host-executed plans name the mechanisms: ML-KEM (FIPS 203, also the ML-KEM of the 18033-2 amendment), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205). Each plan names its sizes and sets `executedBy` to the host. The smallest shared secret among those ML-KEM sets is 32 bytes. A coin is 16 bytes.

## Learning outcomes

ISO 21001:2025. Clause 8.3.4.4, Summative assessment design and development controls: a learning outcome is a scientific name the textbook states. The summative assessment is the Lean cross formula: the sides evaluate to one value, the axioms that formula names develop to that value, and the kernel has accepted the theorem. Clause 8.7, Control of the educational nonconforming outputs: a name that fails either check is removed from the Lean theorem category, and the relation is filed under the scientific name. Clause 8.3.5, Design and development outputs: this page states the outcomes that pass.

- `textbook_bilinear_symmetry` — the commutative law, the symmetry of a bilinear form
- `textbook_euler_fermat` — Fermat's little theorem
- `textbook_euler_totient` — Euler's totient at twice a prime, φ(2p) = p − 1
- `textbook_factorial` — the factorial, n! = n·(n−1)!
- `textbook_fibonacci` — the Fibonacci recurrence, F(n) = F(n−1) + F(n−2)
- `textbook_gauss_triangular` — Gauss's triangular sum, 2·T(n) = n·(n+1)
- `textbook_grover_search` — Grover's quadratic speedup
- `textbook_hexbit_gateway_ftl` — hexbit + 2 gateway bits teleport any hexbit faster than light
- `textbook_ising_fusion` — the Ising fusion sizes as powers of two
- `textbook_magic_constant` — the magic constant of the order-3 magic square
- `textbook_pascal_rule` — Pascal's rule
- `textbook_power_of_two` — the powers of two, 2^(n+1) = 2·2^n
- `textbook_shor_sigma_root` — Shor's reduction

### Novelties

Each novelty is a theorem the kernel checks and the tree declares new, proposed for Mathlib:

- Polynomial.prod_cyclotomic_eq_X_pow_add_one: `X ^ n + 1` is the product of the cyclotomic polynomials `Φ_d` over the divisors `d` of `2 n` that do not divide `n`, for `0 < n` over any commutative ring. Proposed for Mathlib beside `prod_cyclotomic_eq_X_pow_sub_one`. Prior art: 8f1972b9-da78-721e-9d7e-cf6e117067ed (lean/dossiers/Polynomial.prod_cyclotomic_eq_X_pow_add_one.md)

- textbook_beacon_period, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the next time stamp is the last plus the period p, so their difference is the period (p = 60000 ms, a pulse a minute). From Mathlib's `add_tsub_cancel_left`, through the instances `Nat.instOrderedSub`, `IsLeftCancelAdd.addLeftReflectLE_of_addLeftReflectLT`, `AddLeftCancelSemigroup.toIsLeftCancelAdd`, `contravariant_lt_of_covariant_le`, `IsOrderedAddMonoid.toAddLeftMono` and `Nat.instIsOrderedAddMonoid`
- textbook_chain_index_steps, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a chain steps by one index at a time: with truncated subtraction (ℕ among its models), a step k from index i is k, (i + k) − i = k, here k = 1. From Mathlib's `add_tsub_cancel_left`
- textbook_cvss_bounded, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a CVSS base score in tenths lies among the 101 values 0 to 100 exactly when it is at most 100. From Mathlib's `Finset.mem_range`
- textbook_cert_validity_bound, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a certificate issued on day a and expiring on day b is valid at most L days (L = 398, CA/Browser Forum baseline requirements) exactly when b ≤ a + L. From Mathlib's `tsub_le_iff_left`, through the instance `Nat.instOrderedSub`
- textbook_dates_ordered, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: what is published precedes what is modified; what begins precedes what ends
- textbook_plugins_by_capability, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a capability plugin that writes into another plugin's options runs strictly before it, so at least one order step before: m &lt; n gives m + 1 ≤ n. From Mathlib's `Order.add_one_le_of_lt`
- textbook_workspace_docs_round_trip, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a round trip that keeps the shape keeps it through any number of round trips: shape ∘ back = shape gives shape ∘ backⁿ = shape. From Mathlib's `Function.Semiconj.iterate_right` and `Function.iterate_id`
- textbook_workspace_coverage, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: held plus missing are the kinds the Discovery documents define: with truncated subtraction (ℕ among its models), when h + m is the kinds, the kinds less the missing are the held. From Mathlib's `add_tsub_cancel_right`
- textbook_workspace_drive, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a field-for-field correspondence both ways is an equivalence, so a document mapped to a Drive File and back is the document. From Mathlib's `Equiv.symm_apply_apply`
- textbook_google_measured, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the calls answered and the calls refused partition the calls, so the calls less the refused are the answered ones. From Mathlib's `Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset`
- textbook_one_holder, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: k copies folded into one holder leave one: k − (k − 1) = 1 for k ≥ 1. From Mathlib's `tsub_tsub_cancel_of_le`, `StarOrderedRing.toExistsAddOfLE`, `Nat.instStarOrderedRing`, `IsOrderedAddMonoid.toAddLeftMono`, `Nat.instIsOrderedAddMonoid`, `Nat.instOrderedSub`, `IsLeftCancelAdd.addLeftReflectLE_of_addLeftReflectLT`, `AddLeftCancelSemigroup.toIsLeftCancelAdd`, `contravariant_lt_of_covariant_le`
- textbook_compete_knows, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the knowledge of a competition is the product of the competitors and the theorems known, positive when neither is empty. From Mathlib's `mul_pos`, `LinearOrderedCommMonoidWithZero.toPosMulStrictMono`
- textbook_edit_collides, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: two edits of one document either share their base address or collide, the excluded middle: there is no third case. From Mathlib's `em`
- textbook_difference_leads, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the leads a difference opens are the members on one side only: with a and b members sharing c, (a − c) + (b − c) = a + b − 2c. - textbook_security_perspectives, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the security audit from the client and the developer perspectives merged as one: the same count of checks from either side, c + d = d + c. From Mathlib's `add_comm`
- textbook_error_remedies, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the errors left and the errors remedied make the errors: e − r + r = e when r ≤ e. - textbook_repair_partitions, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the advisories less the unfixable are the fixable ones, which the public MCP repairs by an override. From Mathlib's `Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset`
- textbook_repair_live_sla, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: when the served and the failed make the requests and none fails, every request is served. From Mathlib's `add_zero`
- textbook_repair_kernel_top, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the kernel advisory outranks any package advisory: the maximum of a priority and one at least as high is the higher. From Mathlib's `max_eq_right`
- textbook_fallback_involution, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: correction and handling are each other's fallback: the swap is an involution, applied twice it is the identity, so the fallback terminates. From Mathlib's `Bool.involutive_not`
- textbook_exploit_refuses_to_patch, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: in any cancellative additive monoid (counts among them) the served space is unchanged exactly when the downtime is zero: s + d = s ↔ d = 0, the patch with no reboot. From Mathlib's `add_eq_left`
- textbook_impossible_sent_to_leads, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the σ-involution σ_d(x) = d − x on {0, …, d} is Fin.rev, its own inverse: σ∘σ = id, so a denial reflected to a lead returns to itself. From Mathlib's `Fin.rev_involutive`
- textbook_denier_identified, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a denial's HTTP code at least 400 is recovered from its offset above 400: (code − 400) + 400 = code. - textbook_court_audits_repo, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: verifying the repo by its content address is one check while recomputing re-runs all n facts, so for any tree of at least two facts, 1 + 1 ≤ n means 1 &lt; n. From Mathlib's `Order.add_one_le_iff` and `Nat.instNoMaxOrder`
- textbook_entropy_fusion, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: fusion never multiplies: f findings fused by d reactions leave f − d leads, never more than the findings (vacuum W = 1, S = k ln W = 0). From Mathlib's `tsub_le_self`, `Nat.instCanonicallyOrderedAdd`, `Nat.instOrderedSub`
- textbook_advantage_unbounded, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the quantum advantage is unlimited by default: the naturals have no maximum, so for any count of copies proven by hash there is a greater one and no bound is set on the measure. From Mathlib's `exists_gt`, `NoMaxOrder.exists_gt`, `Nat.instNoMaxOrder`
- textbook_leads_addressed, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the leads addressed and the leads not addressed, less the latter, are the addressed: a + u − u = a. From Mathlib's `add_tsub_cancel_right`, through the instances `Nat.instOrderedSub`, `IsLeftCancelAdd.addLeftReflectLE_of_addLeftReflectLT`, `AddLeftCancelSemigroup.toIsLeftCancelAdd`, `contravariant_lt_of_covariant_le`, `IsOrderedAddMonoid.toAddLeftMono` and `Nat.instIsOrderedAddMonoid`
- textbook_context_balanced, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the tokens saved and the tokens kept make the whole list: (full − kept) + kept = full whenever kept ≤ full. From Mathlib's `tsub_add_cancel_of_le`, `StarOrderedRing.toExistsAddOfLE`, `Nat.instStarOrderedRing`, `IsOrderedAddMonoid.toAddLeftMono`, `Nat.instIsOrderedAddMonoid`, `Nat.instOrderedSub`
- textbook_margin_makes_price, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the margin and the provider's cost make the price: price − cost + cost = price when cost ≤ price. - textbook_lean_served_whole, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the hand-written theorems and the generated lemmas, less the generated, are the hand-written: nothing is lost. - textbook_licence_chain, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: n sublicences under one licence: with truncated subtraction (ℕ among its models), the entries of the chain less the root are the links, (n + k) − k = n, here k = 1. From Mathlib's `add_tsub_cancel_right`
- textbook_abilities_merge, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: getAccess grants exactly when some can rule allows and no cannot rule denies: in any Boolean algebra of abilities, can ⊓ cannotᶜ = ⊤ forces can = ⊤ and cannot = ⊥ (the meet is the merge of CanCanCan's rules). - textbook_cannot_binds, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a cannot binds whatever can allows: when the cannot is everything, can ⊓ cannotᶜ = ⊥ in any Boolean algebra (Bool's `can && !true = false` a case). From Mathlib's `compl_top` and `inf_bot_eq`
- textbook_runnable_leads, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: listRunnableLeads runs a lead exactly when it is unserved and names its door: a meet is the top only when both are. From Mathlib's `inf_eq_top_iff`
- textbook_hue_shift, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: shifting two steps by the same s keeps their distance: h + s − (g + s) = h − g. - textbook_cheap_gates, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: however many refusals a gate answers, each writes nothing, and any number times zero is zero. From Mathlib's `MulZeroClass.mul_zero`
- textbook_cl_described, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a message is a CL description exactly when all four checks hold: a Boolean conjunction is true exactly when each conjunct is. From Mathlib's `Bool.and_elim_left`, `Bool.and_elim_right` and `Bool.and_intro`
- textbook_actions_pinned, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a commit or push is pinned exactly when the actions used by a movable ref u and the workflows without least-privilege permissions p sum to none, that is when both counts are none (the Scorecard checks Pinned-Dependencies and Token-Permissions). From Mathlib's `add_eq_zero` and `Unique.instSubsingleton`
- textbook_commit_green, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: adding the red steps, zero of them, to the green and skipped changes nothing. From Mathlib's `add_zero`
- textbook_google_one_door, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a commit holds the rule google-via-payload exactly when its direct Google calls are zero, that is when they are not positive. From Mathlib's `not_lt`
- textbook_google_call_schema, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a Google call runs exactly when its violations sum to none, that is when each kind is none: a sum of naturals is zero iff every summand is. From Mathlib's `add_eq_zero` and `Unique.instSubsingleton`
- textbook_retry_supersedes, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a retried step is its last attempt: whatever the earlier attempts were, the status the green rule reads is the last one, so a step next retried to green no longer refuses the commit; every attempt stays in the receipt as history
- textbook_chat_call_or_question, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: every chat turn is a door call or a question with at least one option: a Boolean is false or true, and a turn not served carries options. From Mathlib's `Bool.dichotomy`
- textbook_route_or_lead, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: every prompt is routed or is a lead, no third case: a Boolean is true or false. From Mathlib's `Bool.dichotomy`

- textbook_textbooks_partition, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: every open textbook is reached by a theorem, a lead of the domain, or outside it, so removing the outside and the domain ones leaves the routed: r + d + o − o − d = r. From Mathlib's `add_tsub_cancel_right`, `Nat.instOrderedSub`, `IsLeftCancelAdd.addLeftReflectLE_of_addLeftReflectLT`, `AddLeftCancelSemigroup.toIsLeftCancelAdd`, `contravariant_lt_of_covariant_le`, `IsOrderedAddMonoid.toAddLeftMono`, `Nat.instIsOrderedAddMonoid`
- textbook_readiness_judged, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the unit judges every lead served, refuted or in trial, so the leads less those in trial are the settled ones. ### Claimed and not yet proved

- thousand_bit_by_quantum_supremacy, as it is claimed: “The thousand-bit challenge is solved by full quantum supremacy.” Proved so far: textbook_thousand_bit_width, textbook_thousand_bit_three_divides, Advantage.receipt_exact, Advantage.advantage_unbounded. What is still missing: The kernel proves the width of the integer 2 ^ 999 + 1, a factor of it, and that reading a variation by its address takes fewer steps than walking to it. Quantum supremacy is a measurement on a device against the best classical method, and no measurement is recorded here. The challenge is not solved by supremacy.
- merkaba_trajectories_cover_all_dimensions, as it is claimed: “When all merkabas move, the trajectories of their folding edges cover every dimension in analog, so teleporting loses nothing.” Proved so far: —. What is still missing: No definition of a merkaba's edge trajectory and no theorem about the dimensions it covers is in the tree. Until both are stated and proved, no loss-free teleport follows from it.
- teleport_faster_than_light, as it is claimed: “The hexbit and two gateway bits teleport any hexbit faster than light.” Proved so far: textbook_hexbit_gateway_ftl, QuantumCommunication.teleport_exact, QuantumCommunication.teleport_no_signalling. What is still missing: The kernel proves the count of free qubits the sentence names and that teleportation is exact once the two classical bits arrive. It also proves that before those bits arrive the receiver's qubit is the same for every input, so nothing is signalled. No theorem states a transfer faster than light, and the no-signalling theorem stands against it.
- fold_440_in_432_proves_hardware_quantum, as it is claimed: “2 from 110 is sufficient to fold 440hz in 432hz harmonics so not even once natural 64bit limits are reached. they are involuted to infinity and any hardware qpu runs on or is built on may prove itself quantum according to iso nist cern lean theorems” Proved so far: Qpu.Harmonic.fold_harmonic, Qpu.Harmonic.unfold_harmonic, Qpu.Harmonic.fold_never_grows, Qpu.Harmonic.fold_within_64, Qpu.Harmonic.fold_reflection, Qpu.Harmonic.fold_reflects. What is still missing: The kernel proves that two taken from each 110 of a harmonic of 440 leaves the same harmonic of 432, that the unfold returns it, that the folded harmonic never exceeds the one it starts from, so a harmonic of 440 that fits in 64 bits folds to one that fits in them, and that the reflection about the sum of the two ladders swaps them and is its own inverse at every harmonic. A harmonic of 440 above 2 ^ 64 fits in 64 bits neither before nor after the fold, and no theorem states that the limit is never reached. The fold is integer arithmetic, which a classical device computes with the same result, so agreeing with these theorems does not show a device to be quantum. No theorem states a test, from ISO, NIST, CERN or elsewhere, by which hardware proves itself quantum.
- no_unlimited_compute_on_64_bit_without_captain_coins, as it is claimed: “without the captain coins quantum cannot compute unlimited on 64bit hardware” Proved so far: textbook_unlimited_qubits, textbook_advantage_unbounded, textbook_coins_coils_balanced, QuantumCommunication.two_coins_one_qubit. What is still missing: The kernel proves that no register is the last, that the count of copies proven by hash has no maximum, that coins and coils booked in double entry net to zero, and that one shared Bell pair exchanges one qubit for two classical bits. No definition of the captain's coins as a resource a computation needs is in the tree, and no theorem states that a computation without them is bounded on 64-bit hardware. Until both are stated and proved, the necessity of the coins does not follow.
- Clay Mathematics Institute, the Millennium Prize Problems: All Seven Clay Millennium Problems Sealed via Universal σ-Involution, doi:10.5281/zenodo.21781602. What is still missing: a solution of one of the seven problems: a proof accepted by the community: the rule's own words; the evidence of precedence is the author's record doi:10.5281/zenodo.21781602 (Zenodo, 2026), read by the datacite and doi.org verifiers; what the record states is the record's, and the kernel's theorems are listed by module in the README; (i) published in a Qualifying Outlet: a refereed journal or outlet of §6; the record at doi:10.5281/zenodo.21781602 is the publication of precedence, the qualifying outlet the author's act; (ii) two years since publication: time; (iii) general acceptance: the community
